description: Built-in AI documentation improvement templates. CANONICAL SOURCE OF TRUTH for README section contracts: each readmeTemplate's requiredSections is authoritative, and other configs (doc-standards.json, repo-structure-standards.json) reference these rather than redefining sections. All guidance assumes semantic compression: high information density, low filler, low repetition. The heuristic provider uses requiredSections to compute estimated score movement and to scaffold missing sections offline; the OpenAI/Anthropic providers fold guidance + requiredSections into the model instruction.

readmeContract.description: Sections required of EVERY README regardless of profile. Computed as the intersection of all readmeTemplate.requiredSections. Consumers that do not know a repo's profile should validate against these.

readmeTemplates.label: Product README
readmeTemplates.summary: Outcome-first README aimed at end users evaluating or adopting the project.
readmeTemplates.guidance: Rewrite for prospective users. Open with a one-paragraph value proposition, then quick-start installation and usage. Use semantic compression: high information density, short sections, low repetition. Preserve accurate badges, links, and license references.

readmeTemplates.label: Developer / Operator README
readmeTemplates.summary: Contributor-facing README emphasizing local setup, architecture, and operations.
readmeTemplates.guidance: Rewrite for developers/operators who will run, extend, or maintain the project. Prioritize prerequisites, local setup, build/test commands, architecture, and troubleshooting. Use semantic compression: compact but executable steps, command-first formatting, no filler.

readmeTemplates.label: Open-Source README
readmeTemplates.summary: Community-ready README with contribution, support, and conduct signals.
readmeTemplates.guidance: Rewrite to meet open-source community expectations. Make purpose obvious, document installation and usage, and surface contribution, support, conduct, security, and license signals. Use semantic compression: concise community-facing docs, strong signal, minimal repetition.

readmeTemplates.label: Portfolio Showcase README
readmeTemplates.summary: Polished README that frames the repo as portfolio evidence of skills.
readmeTemplates.guidance: Rewrite as portfolio evidence. Highlight the problem, technical approach, notable engineering decisions, and skills demonstrated. Use semantic compression: skimmable sections, high evidence density, and placeholders for screenshots/links only where useful.

roadmapTemplates.label: Release-Oriented Roadmap
roadmapTemplates.summary: Roadmap organized into bounded, shippable releases with status.
roadmapTemplates.guidance: Rewrite into bounded, numbered releases. Each release needs a clear goal, compact checkbox milestones, acceptance criteria, and explicit status. Use semantic compression: dense action-first milestone text, no backlog sprawl. Preserve genuinely completed work as completed.

roadmapTemplates.label: Roadmap Contract Format
roadmapTemplates.summary: Standards-compliant roadmap contract suitable for agent dispatch.
roadmapTemplates.guidance: Rewrite to the Roadmap Contract Standard: status header, release index, active-release snapshot, per-release goals, checkbox milestones with implementation-state vocabulary, acceptance criteria, and out-of-scope notes. Use semantic compression and selector-friendly wording so an agent can choose the next task unambiguously.

roadmapTemplates.label: Agent-Dispatch-Ready Roadmap
roadmapTemplates.summary: Roadmap tuned for autonomous selection of high-value next work.
roadmapTemplates.guidance: Rewrite so an autonomous agent can identify the single highest-value next task. Each pending item must be concrete, independently executable, verification-ready, and phrased with semantic compression. Add value/priority signals where missing; keep per-release token footprint low.

roadmapTemplates.label: Recovery / Repair Roadmap
roadmapTemplates.summary: Roadmap that reconstructs structure for a weak or missing plan.
roadmapTemplates.guidance: Rewrite to repair a weak, stale, or missing plan. Infer bounded releases from current repo state, separate completed vs pending work, and establish a forward path with acceptance criteria. Use semantic compression. Do not invent completed history; mark uncertain work as proposed.
